memories.author: D03
memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: 88‑year‑old woman reports retrosternal burning after meals for 2 weeks, occasional sour taste, no dysphagia or weight loss.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/82 mmHg, weight 58 kg, BMI 22.9 (normal). Abdomen soft, non‑tender, no hepatomegaly.
IMPRESSION: Gastro‑oesophageal reflux disease, mild. No alarm symptoms.
ARRANGEMENTS: Start pantoprazole 40 mg OD before breakfast, domperidone 10 mg BD before meals, antacid gel SOS. Advise small frequent meals, avoid lying down after food, weight‑neutral diet. Return if: worsening pain, vomiting, haematemesis, melena, fever >39°C.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Patient reports severe rash and itching after taking penicillin as a child; avoids all beta‑lactams.

memories.author: lab

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Persistent heartburn despite PPI, now 3‑4 days/week, worse after spicy food.
EXAMINATION: BP 140/84 mmHg, weight 57.5 kg, BMI 22.6 (normal). No abdominal tenderness.
IMPRESSION: GERD partially responsive; consider dose optimisation.
ARRANGEMENTS: Increase pantoprazole to 40 mg BD before breakfast and dinner; continue domperidone 10 mg BD; lifestyle reinforcement. Return if: dysphagia, odynophagia, unexplained weight loss, bleeding, fever >39°C.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Message via clinic app: ‘Heartburn is worse at night, waking me up; I’ve started using extra antacid gel.’

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Resting ECG: Normal sinus rhythm, rate 78 bpm. No ST‑T changes, no left ventricular hypertrophy. No evidence of ischemia.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Nighttime heartburn improved but still 2‑3 episodes/week; reports mild bloating.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/80 mmHg, weight 57 kg, BMI 22.4 (normal). Abdomen soft.
IMPRESSION: GERD controlled on BD PPI; consider stepping down after symptom‑free period.
ARRANGEMENTS: Reduce pantoprazole to 40 mg OD before breakfast; continue domperidone 10 mg BD; antacid gel SOS. Advise elevation of head of bed, avoid late meals. Return if: recurrent severe pain, vomiting, bleeding, fever >39°C.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Follow‑up visit; reports occasional heartburn after large meals, otherwise well.
EXAMINATION: BP 136/78 mmHg, weight 56.8 kg, BMI 22.2 (normal). No abdominal tenderness.
IMPRESSION: GERD well‑controlled on low‑dose PPI.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue pantoprazole 40 mg OD, domperidone 10 mg BD, antacid gel SOS. Annual fasting lipid profile and fasting blood sugar ordered today. Return if: new dysphagia, odynophagia, weight loss, bleeding, fever >39°C.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Referral to Dr S. Rao, Gastroenterology, St. Mary’s Hospital, for upper GI endoscopy to rule out Barrett’s esophagus given age >85 and long‑standing GERD, despite symptom control.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Gastroenterology report: Upper endoscopy shows mild erythema in distal esophagus, no Barrett’s metaplasia, no ulcers. Biopsy negative for dysplasia. Advise continue PPI lifestyle measures; repeat endoscopy in 3 years if symptoms persist.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Fasting lipid profile: Total cholesterol 4.2 mmol/L (ref <5.2), LDL 2.1 mmol/L (ref <2.6), HDL 1.4 mmol/L (ref >1.0), triglycerides 1.1 mmol/L (ref <1.7).
Fasting blood sugar: 5.6 mmol/L (ref 3.9‑5.5) – slightly elevated, advise lifestyle.
